strengths: QuEST addresses an important deployment problem with a coherent approach: selectively finetuning time-embedding and attention-related weights, jointly optimizing activation scales, and sharing quantization parameters across neighboring timesteps. Calibration uses teacher-generated samples without requiring the original training images.

The strongest results are substantial improvements in low-bit unconditional generation. In Table 3, W4A4 FID improves over EfficientDM from 10.60 to 5.64 on LSUN-Bedrooms and from 14.34 to 11.76 on LSUN-Churches. These are meaningful empirical gains.

Evaluation covers four models and three generation settings, generally using 50,000 generated images. Stable Diffusion produces recognizable W4A4 outputs and achieves a CLIP score of 28.85, whereas the evaluated Q-Diffusion baseline fails. This demonstrates useful progress despite remaining quality degradation.

The activation-distribution visualizations, layer-sensitivity experiments, and loss/component ablations provide useful evidence for the design. The manuscript cites its datasets, pretrained models, and principal baselines, supplies a code link, and identifies relevant potential effects on watermarking and safety checking.
weaknesses: The theoretical justification is unsound as written. In Section 2.3.1, the stated MSE is quadratic in the final activation, so its second-order Taylor expansion is exact regardless of perturbation magnitude; large perturbations therefore do not establish Proposition 2.1. Furthermore, Equation 5 replaces Equation 10's local epsilon-based quadratic term with an output-residual quadratic without justification. The derivation does not prove that updating the selected weights suffices to control quantization error. This undermines an explicit theoretical contribution, although it does not invalidate the empirical results.

The experiments do not adequately isolate the distinctive benefit of selective, progressive finetuning. Table 7 establishes incremental gains on one W4A8 model, but provides no comparable-budget alternative layer selection, joint-versus-progressive optimization, or direct comparison against LoRA under matched conditions. Corresponding ablations at W4A4, the central challenging setting, are particularly important.

The efficiency advantage over the closest finetuning baseline remains insufficiently established. Table 7 compares only against Q-Diffusion: training time decreases from 23.08 to 15.25 GPU-hours, but memory increases from 10,334 to 12,450 MB. There is no matched time/memory comparison with EfficientDM or measured low-bit inference latency. Thus, the evidence supports a narrower efficiency claim than the manuscript presents.

The limits of the generation-quality evidence need clearer treatment. On W4A4 ImageNet, QuEST has worse sFID and IS than EfficientDM: 7.93 versus 7.75 and 202.45 versus 250.90. Its lower FID is not persuasive evidence of superiority given the manuscript's own discussion of that metric. For Stable Diffusion, CLIP score and two illustrated prompts establish recognizable semantics but provide limited assessment of visual fidelity; an additional quality evaluation and comparison with a finetuning baseline would strengthen the central result.

Important implementation details remain underspecified, including the exact selected layers for each architecture, quantizer granularity and gradient treatment, and conditioning used to generate calibration samples. The headline 'full 4-bit' wording also needs qualification: page 2 retains 8-bit first/last layers and attention matrix multiplications. This precision-label correction does not negate the contribution, but an explicit precision specification is necessary for reproducibility and fair comparison.
